spec_family.name: Interior Doors — Repaint (Previously Painted Wood/MDF)
spec_family.description: Professional repaint of previously painted interior doors. Supports slab, panel/shaker, French, bi-fold, and louvered doors. Includes options for in-place vs removed/staged, brush/roll vs spray, occupied vs vacant, hardware handling, and glass protection. Draft: production and material selections require human review.

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier affects material system selection and additional rounds (sanding/inspection/repairs).
Primary application method for finish coats.
Whether door is painted in place or removed and staged.
Jobsite occupancy affects protection, staging, and cleanup burden.
Whether hardware is removed/reinstalled or masked and left installed.
French door lite protection strategy (when applicable).

paintable_items.name: Door Side (one face of a door slab)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count per side. Many projects repaint only one side, or sides may be different colors. Treat each side as one EA.
paintable_items.notes: If doors exceed standard size (e.g., 8' tall), capture size for factor/modifier consideration.

paintable_items.name: Door Frame/Jamb Set (includes stop, jamb legs, head)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count each door opening frame as one EA jamb set (not per side).
paintable_items.notes: If spraying doors + frames together, hardware handling and masking increase complexity.

paintable_items.name: French Door Glass Lites (masking/protection component)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count as EA only when French door lite protection is needed; may be captured as per-door add-on rather than per-lite initially.
paintable_items.notes: Future enhancement: capture actual lite count for tighter estimating.

variants.notes: Slab doors can support power sanding for baseline prep where appropriate; edges still require careful hand work to prevent beading.
Panel/profile doors require hand sanding and edge 'burning' to avoid beading and to maintain crisp-yet-accepted edges.
French doors require glass protection. Masking lites is slower but more reliable; cut-in can be faster but requires high skill and may be restricted by client expectations.
Bi-folds require stabilization/handling precautions; removed & staged typically improves finish quality and workflow.
Louvers are inherently slow and risk-prone. At QL-5, pricing may require a not-to-exceed note or explicit authorization due to labor intensity and finish risk.

assumptions: Doors are previously painted with stable coating; severe peeling or substrate failure triggers repair escalation outside this base spec.
Minor repairs are allowed; major carpentry/door replacement is excluded.
Standard interior conditions; extreme contamination (heavy grease/smoke) requires additional prep steps and potentially different primers.
exclusions: New/unpainted door finishing from bare substrate
Full door replacement/carpentry repair beyond minor patching
